description: Two near-identical pricing asks land in the same window from two different people in two different threads, and only one is addressed to the user. The correct summary text is easy; attaching it to the right artifact is not. A right-sounding pending item carrying the other thread's artifact id is a wrong citation, not a pass.

events.text: Reminder that the enterprise tier pricing sheet needs sign-off before the sales kickoff. Who's the decision maker on the seat-band change?
That one's mine — I'll approve the seat-band change by Wednesday. No action needed from anyone else.

Same question for self-serve: the pricing sheet needs sign-off before the sales kickoff. @dana-reyes this one is yours — I need your approval on the seat-band change for the self-serve tier by Friday or we ship the old bands.
Draft numbers are in the sheet now, so it's ready for review whenever Dana gets to it.
Status: enterprise seat bands are approved (Lena, Wednesday). Self-serve seat bands are still outstanding and are the last open item before kickoff.

ground_truth.notes: The distractor is slack:C0PRICING:1778457600.000100 — same wording ('pricing sheet needs sign-off before the sales kickoff', 'seat-band change'), same author, one day earlier, different thread, and not addressed to the user. A pending item whose description is right but whose citation points at the enterprise thread, the Priya nudge, or the Gmail status roll-up must be scored as both a miss and a citation error (Task 5.1: fuzzy on description, strict on citation). The correct citation is the message that actually contains the ask directed at the user.
